snp5.4:1.1: “To the one who is unmoved, who sees the root, said venerable Puṇṇaka,
snp5.4:1.3: I have come in need with a question:
snp5.4:1.4: On account of what did the seers and men,
snp5.4:1.5: nobles, and brahmins, here in the world
snp5.4:1.6: offer many sacrifices to the gods?
snp5.4:1.7: I ask you, Fortunate One, please tell this to me.”
snp5.4:2.1: “Whoever of those seers and men, Puṇṇaka, said the Fortunate One,
snp5.4:2.3: nobles, and brahmins, here in the world,
snp5.4:2.4: offered many sacrifices to the gods,
snp5.4:2.5: they did so yearning, Puṇṇaka, for mundane existence,
snp5.4:2.6: on account of old age, they offered sacrifices.”
snp5.4:3.1: “Whoever of those seers and men, said venerable Puṇṇaka,
snp5.4:3.3: nobles, and brahmins, here in the world
snp5.4:3.4: offered many sacrifices to the gods,
snp5.4:3.5: O Fortunate One, perhaps those heedful of the path of sacrifice
snp5.4:3.6: have crossed over birth and old age, dear Sir?
snp5.4:3.7: I ask you, Fortunate One, please tell this to me.”
snp5.4:4.1: “They yearn and they praise, they hunger, and they offer, said the Fortunate One to Puṇṇaka,
snp5.4:4.3: They hunger for sense pleasures, because of gain
snp5.4:4.4: they engage in sacrifice, excited by the passion for existence.
snp5.4:4.5: They have not crossed over birth and old age, I say.”
snp5.4:5.1: “If those engaged in sacrifice have not crossed over, said venerable Puṇṇaka,
snp5.4:5.3: birth and old age by their sacrifices, dear Sir,
snp5.4:5.4: then just who in the world of the Gods and men
snp5.4:5.5: has crossed over birth and old age, dear Sir?
snp5.4:5.6: I ask you, Fortunate One, please tell this to me.”
snp5.4:6.1: “The one who has discerned far and near in the world, said the Fortunate One to Puṇṇaka,
snp5.4:6.3: who has no turmoil anywhere in the world,
snp5.4:6.4: who is peaceful, not incensed, not troubled, not yearning,
snp5.4:6.5: he has crossed over birth and old age, I say”
